title: How cancer mortality has been reduced elsewhere

items.text: In the NORDCAN comparison, survival improved least in Finland between 2001–2005 and 2011–2015 (5-year survival +3–4 percentage points, compared with +8–12 in Denmark).
Lung cancer causes the most cancer deaths in Finland, and outcomes are worse than in the other Nordic countries. Reasons include slower access to a doctor and narrower diagnostics in primary care.

sources.title: University of Helsinki: study in Acta Oncologica 2025

items.text: Denmark closed its survival gap with the other Nordic countries through four national cancer plans (2000–2015), patient pathways, public monitoring of waiting times and expanded screening.
A NORDCAN study attributes the improvements to several factors: earlier diagnosis, better treatment, national cancer plans, uniform guidelines and standardised pathways.
In the Dutch-Belgian NELSON trial, low-dose CT screening reduced lung cancer mortality among high-risk men by 24% over ten years.

sources.title: de Koning et al. 2020, New England Journal of Medicine
